original_value: As a system of ranging and positioning based on time transfer, the timekeeping ability of a navigation satellite constellation is a key factor for accurate positioning and timing services. As the timekeeping performances depend on the frequency stability and predictability of satellite clocks, we propose a method to establish a more stable and predictable space time reference, i.e., inter-satellite link time (ISLT), uniting the satellite clocks through inter-satellite links (ISLs). The joint timekeeping framework is introduced first. Based on the weighted average timescale algorithm, the optimal weights that minimize the increment of the ISLT timescale are determined and allocated to the clock ensemble to improve the frequency stability and predictability in both the long and short term. The time deviations with respect to the system time of nine BeiDou-3 satellites through multi-satellite precise orbit determination (MPOD) are used for joint timekeeping evaluation. According to the Allan deviation, the frequency of the ISLT is more stable than the nine satellite clocks in the short term (averaging time smaller than 7000 s), and its daily stability can reach 6 × 10−15. Meanwhile, the short-term (two hours) and long-term (10 h) prediction accuracy of the ISLT is 0.18 and 1.05 ns, respectively, also better than each satellite clock. Furthermore, the joint timekeeping is verified to be robust against single-satellite malfunction.

result.paraphrase: In time-transfer-based ranging and positioning, the timekeeping capability of a navigation satellite constellation is crucial for accurate positioning and timing services. Because timekeeping performance depends on the frequency stability and predictability of satellite clocks, we propose building a more stable and predictable space time reference—inter-satellite link time (ISLT)—by linking the satellite clocks through inter-satellite links (ISLs). First, the joint timekeeping framework is presented. Using the weighted average timescale algorithm, the optimal weights that minimize the growth of the ISLT timescale are derived and assigned to the clock ensemble to enhance frequency stability and predictability over both short and long terms. Time deviations relative to the system time of nine BeiDou-3 satellites, obtained via multi-satellite precise orbit determination (MPOD), are used to evaluate the joint timekeeping. Based on Allan deviation, ISLT frequency is more stable than the nine satellite clocks in the short term (averaging time below 7000 s), and its daily stability can reach 6 × 10−15. In addition, the ISLT prediction accuracy is 0.18 ns over two hours and 1.05 ns over 10 h, both superior to each satellite clock. The joint timekeeping is also shown to be robust against malfunction of a single satellite.
